task_message:
Case V59: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 116x116x82 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case V59 is complete. Summary of what was done:

**Findings**
- T2-weighted axial/coronal/sagittal overview showed a single T2-hyperintense, lobulated soft-tissue mass in the anterior subcutaneous tissue of the limb (patient right), spanning ~32 mm cranio-caudally and ~18–22 mm in the other planes.
- A separate, markedly bright, homogeneous elongated structure lay outside the body contour anterior to the mass — interpreted as a skin-surface marker/superficial vessel, not tumour, and deliberately excluded (rejected candidate C1).

**Segmentation**
- Seeded with three positive points inside the mass on the axial slice through its largest cross-section (v1, 6.1 mL).
- Verified the green outline against the lesion edge on axial slices at the upper/mid/lower levels, plus coronal and sagittal planes; added a corrective positive point at the upper pole (v2, 6.0 mL, single connected component).
- Final review panels (5 slices per plane, including just past each end) showed no lesion tissue beyond the mask and no stray components; the mask was saved with medium confidence (margin blur at the fading inferior edge being the only residual uncertainty).
